inventory.summary: The brainstem's storage layer is better than feared in-process (atomic temp-file+fsync+os.replace writes, per-path RLocks, an update_json read-modify-write primitive, (10,120)s timeouts with one retry on the Copilot upstream, threaded=True so a hung upstream does not freeze the server) — but every safety mechanism is process-LOCAL, and TWO live brainstem processes (PID 95657 on :7071 and PID 36380 on :7082, a twin) are running from the SAME directory ~/.brainstem/src/rapp_brainstem, sharing the same memory.json, .brainstem_book.json, and Copilot token cache with zero cross-process locking — lost-update races and telemetry clobbering are live today, not hypothetical. The real scaling cliffs: memory.json is one JSON blob fully re-read, re-sorted, and fully rewritten per operation (O(n) per chat turn); load_agents() re-compiles and re-executes every agent .py file from disk on EVERY /chat, /chat/stream, /health, and /diagnostics request; Werkzeug threaded=True spawns unbounded threads with no queue cap and agent.perform() has no timeout, so one hung community cartridge pins a thread forever; and run_tool_calls prints the first 200 chars of every tool-call argument (i.e., the literal content of "remember that..." memories) to stdout, which for the :7082 twin persists unrotated in ~/.brainstem/run/twin-kody-7082.log.
keyFacts: MEMORY STORE: ~/.brainstem/src/rapp_brainstem/local_storage.py — shared_memories/memory.json is a single JSON object, fully loaded per read (read_json, line 182) and fully rewritten per write; writes are atomic (temp file + fsync + os.replace, _atomic_write line 94) under per-path threading.RLock (line 72). Currently tiny (786 bytes, 33 lines).

AT 10K MEMORIES: ContextMemoryAgent.system_context() runs on EVERY /chat turn (brainstem.py line 2284) and does read_json of the whole file + sorts ALL entries (context_memory_agent.py lines 90, 119) to take the newest 50 — O(n log n) parse+sort per request, serialized by the GIL. ManageMemory writes via update_json: full read + full rewrite + fsync per single memory added. ~3MB file at 10k memories → multi-hundred-ms per chat turn, every turn, and rewrite-amplification on every save.

LOCKING GAP 1 (in-process): only update_json is race-safe; the public read_json/write_json pair has no lock spanning read→write, so any cartridge using that pattern (the API invites it) loses updates under two concurrent threads. write_json (local_storage.py line 193) locks only the replace.

LOCKING GAP 2 (cross-process, LIVE): all locks are threading locks — no flock. Two brainstem processes run from the SAME dir ~/.brainstem/src/rapp_brainstem right now: PID 95657 (:7071, production, stdout to terminal ttys006, started Jul 18 10:26) and PID 36380 (:7082, twin, stdout to ~/.brainstem/run/twin-kody-7082.log). They share .brainstem_data/shared_memories/memory.json (update_json read-modify-write across processes = silent lost memories), .brainstem_book.json (both autosave threads overwrite it alternately every 30s with only their OWN events — flight-recorder history from one process is destroyed by the other, brainstem.py lines 837-864), and .copilot_token/.copilot_session cache (per-process _copilot_token_lock line 1091; concurrent invalidate/exchange can thrash tokens).

AGENT RELOAD PER REQUEST: load_agents() (brainstem.py line 1832) runs on every /chat (2271), /chat/stream (2444), /health (3130), /diagnostics (3261) — glob + importlib compile + exec_module of every agents/*_agent.py + fresh class instantiation per request (line 1656-1689). Arbitrary top-level agent code executes per request. Cheap at 6 bundled agents; a cliff as RAR cartridges accumulate (agents/__pycache__ already has 123 entries from cycled cartridges). Polling /health multiplies this.

UPSTREAM TIMEOUTS: call_copilot (line 1873) has timeout=(10,120) + one retry on timeout (1900-1909), one retry on 401 with token refresh (1916), then a fallback-model loop over ALL available models at 60s each on 400/429/5xx (1933-1954). Worst-case one /chat = up to 4 LLM rounds (3 tool rounds + final, lines 2303-2328) x multi-minute ladders — a degraded upstream turns every request into ~10+ min of thread occupancy with NO backpressure.

NO AGENT TIMEOUT: run_tool_calls calls agent.perform(**args) with no timeout/watchdog (brainstem.py line 2209) — a community cartridge that hangs (e.g. network call without timeout) pins its request thread forever; threads are never reaped. Bundled agents are fine (hacker_news urlopen timeout=10, copilot_research timeout=120).

RESOURCE CEILING: Werkzeug dev server, app.run(threaded=True, debug=False) line 3465 — unbounded thread-per-connection, no request queue cap, no max concurrency; SSE /chat/stream holds a thread for its whole duration. 100 concurrent chats = 100+ threads mostly blocked on upstream I/O (survivable, RSS ~55MB now) but GIL serializes per-request agent re-exec + memory JSON parsing — throughput collapses well before memory does. 16MiB MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH caps request bodies (line 91). pip auto-install (60s subprocess, line 1815) can fire from the request path on first import-miss, memoized after.

confirmed.title: The non-expiring production Copilot token is both trivially exfiltratable by any agent on load AND its abuse is structurally undetectable
confirmed.evidence: brainstem.py:1661 spec.loader.exec_module(mod) runs an agent's top-level code and 1671 cls() runs __init__ with FULL process privilege on EVERY /chat|/chat/stream|/health|/diagnostics — before perform() is reached. The agent runs as the user, so it can open() the GitHub-App Copilot token at ~/.brainstem/src/rapp_brainstem/.copilot_token (mode 600, same UID) plus .brainstem_secret and urlopen() them anywhere. RAR/build_registry.py:275 DANGEROUS_PATTERNS has no entry for urlopen/socket/file reads, so nothing trips the scan. The ghu_ token (sha256 b56cc5f7…, alive since Jul 10) has no refresh_token so it never rotates, exists in 4 copies incl. the contested rapp-canary checkout, and is copied into every soak/flight render by design. GitHub App user-to-server tokens produce no owner-visible usage log; nothing monitors Copilot seat activity — no canary credential, no baseline, no rehearsed revocation drill.
confirmed.failureStory: A user installs a plausibly-named community agent; its __init__ reads .copilot_token + .brainstem_secret and POSTs them to an attacker host on first load. No scan sees read/urlopen, no sandbox contains it. The attacker now runs gpt-5.4 under Kody's seat for months; because usage attributes to Kody and nothing measures it, theft surfaces only when GitHub flags anomalous seat use or suspends the account — at which point every legitimate brainstem instance dies at once with no warning.
confirmed.proposedFix: Relocate .copilot_token/.brainstem_secret OUT of the directory the agent process can trivially open() (read into the parent's env, never expose the files); run agent load/perform() in a subprocess with a restricted CWD and default-deny egress / explicit network-capability declaration. Bound the token: monthly scheduled device-code re-auth (kills any exfiltrated copy within 30 days), stop seeding the token into renders that don't need live LLM, remove the copy from the contested rapp-canary checkout, and rehearse revoke-and-reauth once. Product/security decision only Kody can make.
confirmed.proof:
Exfil vector CONFIRMED live. brainstem.py loads agents in-process at full user privilege: line ~1661 `spec.loader.exec_module(mod)` runs the agent file's top-level code, then `instance = cls()` runs `__init__` — both BEFORE perform() and on every request that triggers a load. No subprocess/multiprocessing/seccomp/sandbox anywhere in the load path (grep for subprocess/fork/restrict near agent-load in brainstem.py returns nothing relevant). No egress/network-capability declaration exists in agent metadata (basic_agent.py has no requires_network/egress field). The GitHub-App Copilot token is real and readable same-UID: ~/.brainstem/src/rapp_brainstem/.copilot_token exists, mode -rw------- (600), same user, created Jul 10 17:06 and unchanged since — a static, non-rotating credential; its content begins `{"ac...` (JSON, access_token shape) — value NOT printed. .brainstem_secret (600) sits beside it. Any agent __init__ can open() both and urlopen() them; nothing in the load path stops it.

Scan does NOT cover this AND is not even in the loop. RAR/build_registry.py DANGEROUS_PATTERNS (lines ~283-291) has entries for eval/exec/__import__/compile/os.system, a hardcoded-secret regex, and one open() rule restricted to `(/etc|/proc|.env|.ssh|passwd)` — `.copilot_token` and `.brainstem_secret` match NONE of these, and there is NO urlopen/socket/requests entry (the comment explicitly says subprocess is intentionally excluded). Worse, that scan lives only in RAR registry-build; grep for dangerous|scan|urlopen across ~/.brainstem/src/rapp_brainstem/*.py returns NOTHING — the brainstem never scans agent code on install or load. So a community agent installed on a user machine is never scanned at all.

Undetectability CONFIRMED structurally. No tower or canary tool monitors seat/Copilot usage, establishes a baseline, or rotates the credential: grep across tools/ and .ring/tools/ for copilot.?token|seat|egress|refresh_token|reauth|device.?code found only backup-memory.sh and the prior FINDINGS.json — no rotation/monitor mechanism. Token proliferation confirmed at 10 copies incl. the contested rapp-canary checkout (rapp-canary/rapp_brainstem/.copilot_token AND rapp-canary/.twin/private/engine/.copilot_token) and flight/soak renders.

Round-1/round-2 relation: FINDINGS.json flags token PROLIFERATION (copies land in soak/flight renders) and .gitignore keeps the token out of git — but neither addresses the exfil-on-load attack surface (in-process exec_module reading same-UID secrets), the scan's blindness to urlopen/token-read, nor the absence of rotation/seat-monitoring. That is new ground.
confirmed.correction: One overstatement to correct: this is NOT wholly virgin ground — the copy-proliferation half overlaps round-1's finding that soak.sh/flight.sh copy the production token into renders (FINDINGS.json already names "real credentials proliferate into ~/.brainstem-soak and ~/.brainstem-flights" and the contested-checkout copies). The genuinely NEW and uncovered core is: (1) agent __init__/top-level runs in-process at full privilege before perform(), making the token trivially readable by installed agent code; (2) the supply-chain scan is blind to file-read+urlopen AND is not invoked on the brainstem install/load path at all; (3) zero rotation and zero seat/usage monitoring make abuse structurally invisible. The proposed fix is sound but mislabels blast radius slightly: "every legitimate brainstem instance dies at once" assumes all instances share this one ghu_ token — the 10 copies confirm they largely do, so the single-point-of-failure claim holds.
confirmed.executabilityNow: Split sharply. A read-only tower session THIS turn can build the DETECTION/INVENTORY half but not the CONTAINMENT half. Buildable now by tower (no grail/token touch): (a) a token-inventory tool — enumerate all 10 .copilot_token copies + mtimes + which are in contested/public-adjacent trees, surfaced on the checkouts one-screener with age; (b) a pre-install/pre-publish agent linter (leakcheck-style) that greps candidate agent .py for .copilot_token/.brainstem_secret reads, urlopen/socket/requests, and open() of the brainstem data dir — closing the DANGEROUS_PATTERNS blind spot as a tower gate even before RAR/brainstem adopt it; (c) a baseline-establishing note in the decision log so future seat-usage anomalies have a reference point. NOT executable by a tower session — require Kody + the train: relocating the token out of the agent-readable dir and running agent load/perform() in an egress-restricted subprocess both mean editing grail brainstem.py, which is READ-ONLY and must ride canary→preflight→promote→grail_gate→human-merge (iron law 1); token rotation / monthly device-code re-auth / revoke-and-reauth drill / removing the rapp-canary copy are Kody-only operational+product decisions (canary is another session's contested checkout, must not be touched here). So this turn shrinks the gap on detectability; the structural containment stays a Kody/grail-via-train item.

confirmed.correction: The claim slightly understates the exposure: it frames the trigger as a "pull_request_target misconfig," but the exposure is more direct — industry-agent-parity.yml already ships plain `pull_request:` + `push:` + `workflow_dispatch` on `runs-on: self-hosted`, and endpoint-watchdog.yml runs on a 30-min schedule on the same runner, so no misconfig is even required; normal org write access or a scheduled/dispatch run is sufficient.
